items.title: Firmonertinib in advanced non-small cell lung cancer with epidermal growth factor receptor P-loop and αC-helix compressing mutations.
items.abstract: P-loop and αC-helix compressing (PACC) mutations comprise a structurally distinct subgroup of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with limited treatment options. Firmonertinib is a once-daily oral, brain-penetrant, mutant-selective EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor with a unique trifluoroethoxy side chain. Firmonertinib had high anti-proliferative efficacy in EGFR PACC-mutant cells and xenografts. In the phase 1b FURTHER study (NCT05364073), patients with metastatic EGFR PACC-mutant NSCLC randomized to receive first-line firmonertinib 160 mg (n = 25) or 240 mg (n = 22) had confirmed objective response rates (ORRs) of 43% and 68%, median duration of response not reached and 14.6 months, and median progression-free survival of 11.1 and 16.0 months, respectively; treatment-related adverse events led to dose reductions (19% and 24%) and discontinuation (3% and 0%). Intracranial ORR among patients with brain metastases at baseline was 47% (8/17). Results support further study of first-line firmonertinib in patients with EGFR PACC-mutant NSCLC.

items.title: Long-Acting HIV Therapy in African Adults with Adherence Challenges.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In eastern and southern Africa, approximately 1 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and receiving oral therapy do not have viral suppression because of adherence challenges.
METHODS: We conducted a phase 3b, open-label, randomized trial to compare long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine with oral dolutegravir-based therapy among adults with virally suppressed HIV type 1 (viral load, <200 copies per milliliter) and suboptimal adherence or care engagement. The participants were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intramuscular injections of cabotegravir (600 mg) plus rilpivirine (900 mg) every 8 weeks, with the first two injection visits occurring 4 weeks apart, or to continue daily oral dolutegravir-based therapy; baseline drug-resistance testing was not performed. The primary end point was a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter at week 48; noninferiority was assessed with a margin of -10 percentage points. Confirmed virologic failure (two consecutive viral loads of ≥200 copies per milliliter) was a key secondary end point.
RESULTS: A total of 540 participants were enrolled across seven sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda; 537 were included in the primary analysis. At 48 weeks, 244 of 268 participants (91.0%) in the long-acting-therapy group had a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter, as compared with 240 of 269 participants (89.2%) in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.9), which met the criterion for noninferiority. The results of a per-protocol analysis were consistent with those of the primary analysis. Confirmed virologic failure occurred in 5 participants (1.9%) in the long-acting-therapy group and in no participants in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.5). Serious adverse events were reported in 11 of 271 participants (4.1%) who received long-acting therapy and in 8 of 269 participants (3.0%) who received oral therapy (risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.1 to 4.2).
CONCLUSIONS: Among persons with HIV in Africa who have adherence challenges, long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was noninferior to oral dolutegravir-based therapy for maintaining a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; IMPALA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05546242; Pan African Clinical Trials Registry number, PACT202301600757432TMC278LAHTX3005.).

items.title: Phase 2 Trial of Icotrokinra for Patients with Ulcerative Colitis.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monoclonal antibodies targeting the interleukin-23 pathway are effective in treating inflammatory bowel disease. However, these therapies must be administered intravenously or by subcutaneous injection.
METHODS: We conducted a phase 2b, double-blind, randomized trial of oral icotrokinra, a peptide that blocks the interleukin-23 receptor, in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis. Participants were assigned to receive icotrokinra at a once-daily dose of 400 mg, 200 mg, or 100 mg or placebo. The primary end point was clinical response at week 12. Secondary end points included clinical remission, remission of symptoms, and endoscopic improvement at week 12.
RESULTS: A total of 252 participants underwent randomization: 63 were assigned to the 400-mg group, 62 to the 200-mg group, 64 to the 100-mg group, and 63 to the placebo group. All the doses of icotrokinra were superior to placebo with respect to a clinical response at week 12, which occurred in 63% of the participants in the 400-mg group, 58% in the 200-mg group, and 55% in the 100-mg group, as compared with 27% in the placebo group (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo). The percentage of participants with clinical remission at week 12 was also significantly higher in the 400-mg group than in the placebo group (30% vs. 11%, P = 0.006), as were the percentage of participants with symptomatic remission (46% vs. 19%, P<0.001) and the percentage of participants with endoscopic improvement (37% vs. 14%, P = 0.002). Clinical remission at week 12 occurred in 24% of the participants in the 200-mg group (P = 0.054 for the comparison with placebo); in accordance with the fixed-sequence testing procedure to account for multiple comparisons, no further formal testing of secondary end points was conducted. Through week 28, the percentage of participants with adverse events was 60% in the 400-mg group, 66% in the 200-mg group, 66% in the 100-mg group, and 62% in the placebo group. For serious adverse events, the percentages were 2%, 5%, 0%, and 10%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Among participants with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, a clinical response at week 12 was significantly more common with once-daily oral icotrokinra at each of three tested doses than with placebo. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; ANTHEM-UC ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06049017.).

items.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide in high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer: a randomized phase 2 trial.
items.abstract: Combining inhibition of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase and androgen receptor (AR) pathway has demonstrated clinical activity in men with metastatic prostate cancer, although the extent of benefit in tumors lacking homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations remains uncertain. We conducted a randomized phase 2 trial evaluating talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in men with high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer (mHNPC). Fifty-four patients starting androgen deprivation therapy received two cycles of enzalutamide lead-in before 1:2 randomization to enzalutamide (n = 17) or enzalutamide plus talazoparib (n = 37). The primary endpoint was met, with a 73% prostate-specific antigen (PSA) <0.2 ng ml-1 response rate at 12 months in the combination arm (95% confidence interval (CI) = 56-86%), exceeding the prespecified efficacy threshold (P < 0.001); the PSA <0.2 rate in the control arm was 64.7% (95% CI = 38-86%, P = 0.54 for exploratory comparison between arms). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 68% patients receiving the combination versus 35% with enzalutamide alone, predominantly anemia (41%). Two fatal therapy-emergent myeloid neoplasms occurred in the enzalutamide plus talazoparib arm in patients with underlying genomic susceptibility. Analyses of paired tumor biopsies acquired at baseline and during enzalutamide lead-in phase demonstrated marked tumor transcriptional reprogramming after AR inhibition, including suppression of proliferation-associated and HRR-related gene expression programs, but without functional impairment of homologous recombination activity. Overall, talazoparib plus enzalutamide demonstrated clinical activity in patients with high-volume mHNPC but did not establish clear additional clinical benefit over enzalutamide alone in this biomarker-unselected population, while being associated with increased toxicity. items.title: Nivolumab-Ipilimumab for Localized Microsatellite Instability-High Gastric/Gastroesophageal Junction Adenocarcinoma: The Phase 2 NEONIPIGA Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab in localized deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma was evaluated in the NEONIPIGA study. The primary end point of pathological complete response (pCR) was previously reported.
OBJECTIVE: To report long-term follow-up results and secondary end points, including event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS), of the NEONIPIGA study.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The NEONIPIGA study is a French, multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial that included patients with histologically proven cT2-T4NXM0 deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high GEJ adenocarcinoma who were eligible for surgery. Patients were enrolled between October 23, 2019, and June 4, 2021, and the database was locked on November 13, 2025.
INTERVENTION: Neoadjuvant nivolumab, 240 mg, every 2 weeks for 6 cycles plus ipilimumab, 1 mg/kg, every 6 weeks for 2 cycles, followed by surgery 5 weeks after the last nivolumab dose, and adjuvant nivolumab, 480 mg, every 4 weeks for 9 cycles.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: EFS and OS.
RESULTS: A total of 32 patients (median [range] age, 65 [40-80] years; 8 [28%] female and 21 [72%] were male) were included: 16 (50%) with gastric cancer and 16 (50%) with GEJ cancer. Three patients did not undergo surgery (1 with metastatic disease and 2 who refused). Twenty-seven patients (84%) completed neoadjuvant therapy and 14 (44%) received all treatment as planned. Neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapy-related grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 6 (19%) and 4 patients (17%), respectively. Median follow-up was 48.3 months (95% CI, 44.8-52.0 months). Among the 32 patients in the intention-to-treat population, 4-year OS was 84.1% (95% CI, 65.8%-93.0%). In the 31 patients eligible for surgery, 4-year EFS was 83.5% (95% CI, 64.8%-92.8%). One patient relapsed with cerebral metastases. Six deaths occurred: 2 related to gastric cancer or treatment (1 patient had postoperative complications and 1 cerebral metastases) and 4 unrelated. All patients who did not undergo surgery achieved a clinical complete response after immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. One patient subsequently died of causes unrelated to their cancer. Overall, 17 of 29 patients (59%) achieved pCR on surgical specimen. Safety was previously reported, and no additional late toxic effects were observed.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial, the immunotherapy regimen evaluated was associated with sustained long-term survival, but no clear evidence of improved survival over outcomes reported in other studies evaluating surgery alone in this patient population was observed. The high pCR rates and durable responses observed may provide useful information for designing future clinical studies, including randomized trials investigating organ-preserving strategies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04006262.

items.title: Neoadjuvant Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy Before Inferior Vena Cava Thrombectomy for Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Phase 2 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with inferior vena cava (IVC) tumor thrombus is associated with substantial perioperative risk and frequent recurrence despite nephrectomy and thrombectomy. No established neoadjuvant local therapy exists for this high-risk population.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, clinical outcomes, and exploratory biomarker effects of neoadjuvant stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) targeting IVC tumor thrombus before nephrectomy and thrombectomy.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center prospective phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial enrolled patients with newly diagnosed RCC and Mayo level II to IV IVC tumor thrombus eligible for neoadjuvant SABR and definitive surgery from July 2015 to January 2024. Data were analyzed from August 2025 to August 2026.
INTERVENTION: Neoadjuvant SABR to the radiographically defined IVC tumor thrombus, delivered as 40 Gy in 5 fractions or 36 Gy in 3 fractions, followed by radical nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was 1-year recurrence-free survival (RFS) compared with a prespecified historical surgery-alone benchmark of 55.7%. Secondary outcomes included 90-day perioperative morbidity and mortality, adverse events, pulmonary embolism, overall survival, and cancer-specific survival. Exploratory analyses included Ki-67 immunohistochemistry and tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA.
RESULTS: Of 23 patients who received neoadjuvant SABR, 22 completed surgery, and 21 were included in the primary RFS analysis. Of 21 included patients, 12 (57%) were male, and the median (IQR) age was 62.5 (54.0-73.2) years. A total of 19 patients had clear-cell RCC; all tumors were grade 3 or 4, and 3 patients had metastatic disease at enrollment. At a median (range) follow-up of 108.6 (2.0-127.2) months, 1-year RFS was 71.4% (80% CI, 56.6-82.0; 95% CI, 47.2-86.0), meeting the prespecified phase 2 screening criterion based on comparison with the historical surgery-alone benchmark of 55.7% (P = .09). One-year overall survival was 95.2% (80% CI, 83.9-98.7; 95% CI, 70.7-99.3) and cancer-specific survival was 95.2% (80% CI, 83.9-98.7; 95% CI, 70.7-99.3). No 90-day perioperative mortality occurred; 4 grade 4 treatment-attributed events occurred, but no grade 4/5 radiation-attributed toxic effects occurred. Ki-67 expression was reduced in patients with irradiated tumor thrombus compared with nonirradiated controls. Tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA was detected in all patients with available plasma and declined after treatment.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this nonrandomized clinical trial, neoadjuvant SABR before nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy appeared feasible with an acceptable safety profile. RFS met the prespecified phase 2 screening criterion but remains exploratory and warrants further evaluation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02473536.

items.title: Lonvoguran Ziclumeran - In Vivo CRISPR Gene Editing in Hereditary Angioedema.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hereditary angioedema is a rare and potentially life-threatening genetic condition characterized by recurrent and debilitating swelling attacks. Lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z) - an investigational, in vivo gene-editing treatment based on clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) - is being developed as a single-dose treatment for hereditary angioedema.
METHODS: In a phase 3, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned, in a 2:1 ratio, patients who were 16 years of age or older and had hereditary angioedema with C1 inhibitor deficiency to receive a single intravenous infusion of lonvo-z (at a dose of 50 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the number of investigator-confirmed hereditary angioedema attacks per month (the monthly attack rate) from week 5 through week 28 after infusion.
RESULTS: A total of 80 patients underwent randomization; 52 were assigned to receive lonvo-z and 28 to receive placebo. As of February 10, 2026, the median duration of follow-up was 7.5 months (range, 4.9 to 12.8). The least-squares mean monthly attack rate from weeks 5 through 28 was 0.26 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15 to 0.45) in the lonvo-z group and 2.10 (95% CI, 1.55 to 2.86) in the placebo group (relative difference, -87%; 95% CI, -93 to -78; P<0.001). Adverse events that occurred during or after infusion of lonvo-z or placebo were reported in 92% and 86% of the patients in the lonvo-z and placebo groups, respectively, from day 1 through week 28. Among the adverse events that occurred during or after infusion and more often in the lonvo-z group than in the placebo group, the most common (occurring in >10% of the patients in the lonvo-z group) included infusion-related reaction, headache, fatigue, back pain, and upper respiratory tract infection. No serious or grade 3 or higher adverse events were reported in the lonvo-z group.

items.title: EGFR-targeted antibody-toxin conjugate in recurrent glioma: a phase 1 trial.
items.abstract: D2C7-ATC is a recombinant antibody-toxin conjugate (ATC) targeting wild-type epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and mutant EGFR variant III (EGFRvIII). We conducted a single-arm, single-site, open-label phase 1 trial evaluating a single infusion of D2C7-ATC via convection-enhanced delivery in the enhancing disease of 81 patients with biopsy-confirmed recurrent malignant glioma. The primary objective was to determine toxicity and the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of D2C7-ATC. Secondary objectives included describing overall survival (OS) and assessing the association between EGFR expression and OS. The median overall survival (mOS) was 7.9 months among 72 patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type recurrent glioblastoma (IDHwt rGBM), including 35 patients in the dose-escalation stage (40 to 35,032 ng ml-1) and 37 patients in the dose-expansion stage (RP2D of 6,920 ng ml-1). D2C7-ATC was generally well tolerated, with mainly grade 1-2 treatment-related adverse events (67%). The maximum tolerated dose was exceeded at 35,032 ng ml-1, where four patients experienced dose-limiting toxicities, including grade 4 (N = 2) and grade 3 (N = 2) events. Eight patients died on trial; all deaths were unrelated to D2C7-ATC. Univariate analyses identified survival-associated biomarkers, including tumor D2C7 antibody reactivity, circulating cytokines, a tumor inflammatory gene signature and neutrophils, monocytes and lymphocytes in blood. Notably, patients with IDHwt rGBM with a D2C7 antibody reactivity score of <1.5+ in pre-treatment tumor had an mOS of 17.38 months, whereas those with low IL-8 in post-treatment plasma had an mOS of 16.6 months. These findings indicate that EGFR-targeted D2C7-ATC therapy prolongs survival in a subset of patients with IDHwt rGBM via intratumoral and systemic immune activation. items.title: Ponatinib-Blinatumomab or Imatinib-Chemotherapy for Adult Ph-Positive ALL.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The outcome of Philadelphia-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph-positive ALL) has greatly improved with the use of tyrosine kinase inhibitors and immunotherapy.
METHODS: In this trial, we randomly assigned adult patients with Ph-positive ALL in a 2:1 ratio to receive ponatinib plus blinatumomab (intervention group) or imatinib plus chemotherapy (control group) as frontline treatment. A crossover to the intervention group was allowed for patients with persistence or reappearance of measurable residual disease in the control group. The primary end point was event-free survival.
RESULTS: A total of 236 patients underwent randomization: 158 to the intervention group and 78 to the control group. The median age of the patients was 55 years (range, 24 to 82). At a median follow-up of 23.7 months, the estimated 24-month event-free survival was 86% in the intervention group and 67% in the control group (P<0.001). Survival with no measurable residual disease was 68% and 42%, respectively. At the end of induction, a complete hematologic response was observed in 94% of the patients in the intervention group and in 79% of those in the control group. After blinatumomab consolidation, a molecular response was observed in 71% and 49% of the patients, respectively. After crossover to the intervention group, 20 of 31 patients (64%) had a molecular response. Overall survival was 90% in the intervention group and 85% in the control group. The cumulative incidence of relapse was 5% and 13%, respectively. As of this report, only 19% of the patients in the intervention group had undergone hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation after having had a first complete hematologic response.
CONCLUSIONS: In this phase 3 trial, a frontline chemotherapy-free targeted and immunotherapeutic approach was superior to the use of imatinib and chemotherapy. (Funded by Associazione Italiana per la Ricerca sul Cancro and others; GIMEMA ALL2820 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04722848.).

items.title: Real-world, digital-first delivery of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in women.
items.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. Among participants with paired biomarker data, mean glycated hemoglobin decreased by 3.3 mmol mol-1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P < 0.001), normalizing in 84.5% of those with baseline diabetes-range values and 96.3% with prediabetes, and lipid parameters improved significantly (reductions in total cholesterol of 0.77 mmol l-1, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l-1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l-1). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

items.title: Infant hippocampal and amygdala volume in an observational follow-up from a randomized clinical trial for maternal prenatal depression.
items.abstract: Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group (p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

items.title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks.
items.abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1-7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In 'low-dosage' villages (in which 5-30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50-100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated-treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated-untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals' connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable.

items.title: TRANSFORM-1 phase 3 study: efficacy and safety of navitoclax plus ruxolitinib in patients with untreated myelofibrosis.
items.abstract: The phase 3 TRANSFORM-1 study evaluated ruxolitinib (RUX) in combination with navitoclax (NAV) or placebo (PBO) in Janus kinase inhibitor-naïve adults with intermediate-2 or high-risk myelofibrosis and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of ≤2. Patients were randomized 1:1 to NAV (200 mg/d starting dose, or 100 mg escalated to 200 mg/d) or PBO, with RUX dosed per label. The primary end point was ≥35% spleen volume reduction (SVR) at week 24 (SVR35W24). Secondary end points included change from baseline in total symptom score (TSS) at week 24 and SVR35 at any time. A total of 252 patients (NAV+RUX, n = 125; PBO+RUX, n = 127; median follow-up 20.3 months) were randomized; >80% had intermediate-2 risk, and ∼50% had high-molecular risk disease. SVR35W24 was achieved by 63.2% with NAV+RUX vs 31.5% with PBO+RUX (P< .0001). Mean change in TSS at week 24 was not significantly different between NAV+RUX and PBO+RUX (-10.2 vs -11.6; P = .2852). SVR35 at any time was achieved in 76.8% with NAV+RUX vs 44.1% with PBO+RUX (nominal P< .0001). A ≥20% variant allele frequency reduction (exploratory end point) occurred in 58.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 49.0-67.5) with NAV+RUX and 45.5% (95% CI, 36.4-54.8) with PBO+RUX. NAV+RUX showed higher hematologic toxicity vs PBO+RUX (grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia, 54.0% vs 19.2%; grade 3/4 neutropenia, 40.3% vs 8.8%); diarrhea (any grade, 41.9% vs 16.8%) was also more common. Cytopenias were generally manageable and reversible with dose adjustments. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT04472598.

items.title: STING reprogramming by estrogen promotes neutrophil extracellular trap formation and sex-biased resistance to ADC therapy.
items.abstract: Sex differences in cancer therapy response remain poorly understood. Using a "phase II-like preclinical trial" across 55 CLDN18.2+ pancreatic cancer patient-derived xenografts, we identify marked female-biased resistance to CLDN18.2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) therapy despite equivalent antigen expression. Mechanistically, estrogen signals through GPER1 to upregulate TRAF6, redirecting tumor-intrinsic STING signaling from IRF3-mediated interferon production toward nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) activation. This drives CXCL1 secretion, neutrophil recruitment, and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. NETs form a charged extracellular network that restricts antibody access to tumor-cell-surface antigens-a mechanism we term functional antigen shielding-reducing ADC cytotoxicity independently of antigen expression. The NET burden also correlated with poorer responses to trastuzumab, cetuximab, and enfortumab vedotin across three clinical cohorts. Pharmacologic NET disruption with sivelestat restored ADC efficacy in female mice. These findings reveal an estrogen-driven resistance mechanism with broad implications for antibody-based cancer therapy.

items.title: Personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines in ovarian cancer: a phase 1 trial.
items.abstract: Personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines in the adjuvant setting are of increasing interest across malignancies. Here we report the results of a phase 1 clinical trial testing the feasibility and safety of personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines for high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer. 'NeoVax' consisted of pools of synthetic long peptides targeting patient-specific neoantigens admixed with the immunostimulant poly-ICLC, was combined with delayed administration of anti-PD-1 antibody, and was tested in ten patients (one newly diagnosed patient (Cohort A) and nine patients at first recurrence (Cohort B)) with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer following standard-of-care platinum doublet chemotherapy. Nine of 12 evaluable Cohort B patients were vaccinated (75%, 90% CI 47-93%) and 1 of 9 Cohort A patients (11%, 90% CI 0.6-43%). No unexpected safety signals were encountered and no patients discontinued treatment due to toxicity. Across patients, >70% selected targets remained detectable by noninvasive cell-free DNA analysis despite a median of 6.5 months from the time of diagnostic biopsy to vaccine administration, during which, patients received standard-of-care chemotherapy. Biomarker analysis was suggestive of biologic activity of the vaccine in six of ten patients and this was associated with broader tumor and vaccine-specific immune responses in blood and tumor following vaccination. Resistant tumor clones reflected diverse mechanisms affecting antigen presentation, indicative of immune-selective pressure exerted by vaccination. Overall, the interplay between the repertoire of antigens presented by the tumor and the breadth of induced immunity seemed to dictate clinical efficacy following vaccination.
